analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: The outlook for corporate equity supply and demand in 2027
key_insights: US equity issuance is on track for a record year in 2026. Corporates have raised $431 billion YTD via IPOs, follow-ons, converts and SPACs, up 98% y/y, and GS expects the total to pass the 2021 high of $540 billion. Deal counts and issuance as a share of market cap are close to historical averages, so the dollar total is boosted by a handful of very large deals.

Q3 2026 issuance slowed sharply after a record Q2. Corporates raised $93 billion in Q3, up 20% y/y but down from $252 billion in Q2. Follow-ons were $45 billion and IPOs only $7 billion. September's 19 follow-ons and 5 IPOs were the lowest monthly counts since the April 2025 tariff shock.

Rising rates are a driver of the slowdown. The 10-year Treasury yield is up about 125 bp over the past year and more than 50 bp since late August, mostly from real yields, which is roughly a 2 standard deviation move over 20 years. Sharp rate increases have historically coincided with falling issuance.

Weak market breadth also explains the slowdown. The S&P 500 is within 1% of its all-time high but the median stock is 16% below its high, the narrowest breadth since the Dot-Com Bubble. Adjusting the GS IPO Barometer for breadth cuts it from 146 to 93, slightly below the historical average.

GS forecasts $600 billion of US corporate equity issuance in 2027, made up of $175 billion of IPOs and $425 billion of other primary supply. That equals 0.8% of US equity market cap, in line with the 10-year average and down from about 1% in 2026. The drivers are solid growth, rising equity prices, lower rates and ongoing AI investment.

Equity funds part of the AI buildout. AI-related follow-ons total roughly $65 billion YTD, 45% of US follow-on volume, against roughly $600 billion of AI-related debt issuance. GS expects hyperscaler operating cash flow and debt issuance together to exceed capex in 2027 and 2028, which gives hyperscalers limited reason to issue equity.

Corporate equity demand should offset part of the supply. S&P 500 gross buybacks rose 15% y/y in H1 2026 and YTD authorizations of $1.1 trillion are tracking more than 20% above last year. GS expects buybacks of $1.7 trillion in 2027, up from $1.5 trillion in 2026, and total buybacks plus cash M&A above $2 trillion.

Net US public equity supply in 2027, including expiring lockups, should be the largest since 2000. About $1.7 trillion of shares unlock in 2027. GS says not all unlocked shares will be sold and that much of the proceeds will be reinvested in equities. It does not expect the added supply to derail the bull market.

Household and foreign demand backs the market. Households bought more than $800 billion of equities in H1 2026 and non-US investors more than $350 billion, together over $1 trillion. GS expects continued earnings growth and falling yields to sustain demand.

History suggests large IPOs only pressure the market briefly. The S&P 500 has traded flat on average in the weeks around the largest IPOs of the past 30 years, including SpaceX in June 2026. GS's Sentiment Indicator at -1.3 shows light positioning, so investors have little need to sell to make room for new offerings.

Rising rates could slow buyback growth. The gap between the S&P 500 cost of equity and the cost of debt is one of the narrowest in decades, which makes equity issuance relatively more attractive than debt. GS's base case is falling rates and continued buyback growth. GS credit strategists expect $2.4 trillion of USD IG debt issuance in 2027.

GS S&P 500 forecasts: 7765 current, 8000 year-end 2026, 8700 at 12 months (12% return). GS EPS is $375 for 2026 (+36%) and $415 for 2027 (+11%). Bottom-up consensus is $366 and $422, and top-down strategist consensus is $355 and $410. Forward P/E is 19x.

Rates and macro forecasts: GS rates strategists see the 10-year Treasury falling from 5.2% to 4.4% by year-end 2027, and the 12-month target in the GS macro table is 4.5%. GS expects 2027 corporate earnings growth of 11%. GS macro forecasts also include Brent falling from $104 to $78 and gold rising from $4157 to $5140 over 12 months.

Weekly movers: the best S&P 500 stocks were PTC (+35%), Crown Castle (+20%), Moderna (+18%), Constellation Energy (+16%) and Vistra (+15%). The worst were Mosaic, Teradyne, Skyworks, C.H. Robinson and Deere (each about -10%), with telecom names VZ, TMUS and T down about 9%. The S&P 500 rose 1.3% on the week, led by Consumer Staples (+4.1%) and Energy (+4.0%).

Sector earnings: GS top-down expects Info Tech EPS contribution to rise from $118 to $157 in 2027 (+33%). Communication Services (-18%), Consumer Discretionary (-10%) and Energy (-9%) are forecast to decline in 2027. Concentration is high, with the 10 largest companies at 41% of S&P 500 market cap and 37% of earnings.

market_movers.rationale: NVDA raised its buyback authorization by $150 billion to $235 billion, cited as an example of buyback strength among AI infrastructure companies.

earnings_insights: GS top-down S&P 500 EPS: 2026E $375 (+36% y/y) and 2027E $415 (+11%), versus bottom-up consensus $366 (+33%) and $422 (+15%) and top-down strategist consensus $355 (+29%) and $410 (+15%). These are forecasts, not reported figures.
GS expects 2027 corporate earnings growth of 11%, a forecast.
Sector EPS growth in 2027 (GS top-down forecast): Info Tech +33%, Financials +7%, Health Care +17%, Industrials +16%, Comm Services -18%, Consumer Discretionary -10%, Energy -9%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield is up about 125 bp over the past year and more than 50 bp since late August, mostly from real yields. Rising yields have weighed on equity issuance.
GS rates strategists expect yields to fall, which supports IPO and issuance volumes in 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS describes economic growth as solid, which supports issuance and equity demand.

crypto_views: Bitcoin is shown in Exhibit 40 as one of the weakest YTD assets, with a negative total return and a negative return/volatility ratio. The report does not discuss crypto in the text.
risk_factors: Continued sharp rises in interest rates would hurt equity prices and issuance and could slow buyback growth by narrowing the gap between the cost of debt and the cost of equity.
The largest net public equity supply since 2000 in 2027, from issuance and expiring lockups, adds pressure to equity valuations.
Narrow market breadth lowers the IPO Barometer and signals weakness beneath the index.
Dollar issuance in 2026 is concentrated in a few very large deals, so the totals overstate how broad the issuance boom is.

Top-10 S&P 500 constituents account for 41% of market cap and 37% of earnings.
S&P 500 3-month realized average stock correlation is shown at 0.07 in Exhibit 30.
Trailing 12-month fund flows: equities $345 billion, money markets $516 billion and bonds $837 billion (Exhibit 23).

tension_points.bull_case: Buybacks of $1.7 trillion, cash M&A, household purchases over $800 billion and foreign purchases over $350 billion in H1 2026, plus falling yields and 11% earnings growth, should absorb the supply. Light positioning means investors have room to buy new offerings.
tension_points.bear_case: Net US public equity supply in 2027, including expiring lockups, is the largest since 2000. It adds to pressures on valuations, and rising rates would narrow the cost of debt versus equity gap and slow buyback growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued sharp rise in interest rates, which GS says would restrain buyback growth and weigh on equity prices and issuance.
